description:
FILED s507 (Fable, 2026-10-04), found while checking that a required file ignores its own `#!` line (s506f review).  Loud (the program dies), and the die is trappable -- `eval { require "./M2.pm" }` sets $@ where perl succeeds.

PROBE (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/review/tmp/x/; M2.pm = `package M2; sub v { 7 } 1;`):
  require './M2.pm'; print M2::v(), "B\n";                 perl 7B      PCL: Can't locate ./M2.pm in @INC (@INC contains: …)
  require "./M2.pm"; …                                     perl 7C      PCL: same death
  BEGIN { require "./M2.pm" } …                            perl 7D      PCL: same death
  eval { require "./M2.pm" }; print $@ ? "fail" : "ok";    perl ok      PCL: fail
  require "./t1.pl";  /  do "./M2.pm";  /  my $f = "./M2.pm"; require $f;       work on PCL
  use lib "."; require M2;                                  works on PCL
  Same with and without the script cache (`--no-cache`), and from the file's own directory.
SUSPECT (cheap discriminating measurement, NOT taken): `./pl2cl` on the one-line program -- the literal's `.pm` suffix sends it down the MODULE-name path (`p-require` / a compile-time module lookup that converts the string to a module and searches @INC) while `.pl` takes `p-require-file`; perl's rule is about the PATH, not the suffix: a filename starting with `/`, `./` or `../` is used as given.  Expected fix: the suffix test gives way to the explicit-path test in the one place that chooses between the two lowerings (and in the prototype pre-merge that reads a required module's prototypes, so a `./M2.pm` with a `(&@)` sub still parses its callers).
BREAKING CASES: `require "M2.pm"` (no ./, IS searched in @INC -- with `.` not in @INC since 5.26 it dies in perl too); `require "sub/dir/M.pm"` (searched in @INC as a relative name); `require "../lib/M.pm"`; %INC's key (perl stores the string as given: "./M2.pm"); a second `require "./M2.pm"` is a no-op.


=== DONE (s507b, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-04) ===
The measurement: `./pl2cl` emits `(p-require-file "./M2.pm")`, and the RUNTIME's p-require-file sent every `.pm`
to the module-name path (`./M2` -> module "./M2" -> searched in @INC).  Fix: that delegation now requires a NON-
explicit path (%p-explicit-path-p: `/`, `./`, `../`) -- perl's rule is the PATH; an explicit path takes the literal
arm, %INC keyed by the string as given.  Probe scratch/s507b/m4/q.pl identical to perl: `'./M2.pm'`, `"./M2.pm"`
twice (a no-op), %INC key `./M2.pm` (and no `M2.pm`), BEGIN-time, eval-trapped, a missing `./Nope.pm` (Can't
locate, trappable), `require "M2.pm"` (searched in @INC only: fails, as perl), `./sub/M5.pm`, `../m4/M6.pm`, and a
BEGIN-required `./P.pm` declaring `(&@)` whose caller `P::blk { … } LIST` parses as a block call.
Guard Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t row 91 (fails on 08de9e4f).
subject: (found by a s507 review probe, PRE-EXISTING on 618db500 and main 2e71d4aa): `require "./M2.pm";` -- a LITERAL explicit relative path ending in .pm -- dies "Can't locate ./M2.pm in @INC"; perl loads the file from the current directory (a path starting with ./ or ../ or / is never searched in @INC).  `require "./t1.pl"`, `do "./M2.pm"` and `my $f = "./M2.pm"; require $f` all work
